First Revision )
0. FOREWORD

0.1This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 11 May 1978, after the draft finalized by the Fish and Fisheries Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council.
0.2 Pomfret is a commercially important fish of the Maharashtra, Gujarat After landing, the fish is iced and transported to proand Andhra coasts. Most of the fish is marketed fresh and cessing and consuming centres. The formulation of this standard has been felt necessary with a frozen. view to making available fresh pomfret of desired quality to the consumers. The standard is also intended to serve as a guide for selecting raw materials for frozen pomfrets. 0.3 This standard was first published in 1968. The present revision incorporates a number of modifications, namely : (a) microbiological limits have been incorporated, (b) requirement for washing the fish with potable chlorinated water has been included, and (c) packing requirement has been made more specific. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether standard is complied with, the final value, ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be The number of significant IS: 2-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the a particular requirement of this observed for calculated, expressrounded off in accordance with places retained in the rounded specified value in this standard.

B-2. SCALE B-2.1 Lot -

OF SAMPLING

All the containers in r. single consignment of the material packed on the same day and of the same grade shall constitute a lot. If the consignment is declared to consist of material packed on different dates, the material shxll be separated datewise and the containers of the same grade shall be grouped to constitute a lot. B-2.1.1 Samples shall be tested for each lot for ascertaining of the material to the requirements of this specification. conformity depend

IS : 4780 - 1978 B-2.3 The containers shall be selected at random. In order to ensure randomness of selection a random number table shall be used. If such tables are not available, the following procedure may be adopted.
Starting from any container, count them as 1, 2,3, . . . . . . . . . . up to r in one order. Where r is equal to the integral part of the value of N/n, N being the total number of containers and n the number of containers to be chosen ( see Table 3 ). Every sth containers thus counted shall be separated until the requisite number of containers is obtained from the lot to give samples for test. B-2.4 From each of the selected containers, in order to select at random the required number of fresh pomfrets, Table 3 may be applied. Column may be taken to represent the number of fresh pomfrets in a container and co1 2 may be taken to represent the number of fresh pomfrets to be selected.
